In March 2014, the Redbirds were purchased by their major league parent club, the St. Louis Cardinals.[[11]](#cite_note-2014sale2-11) The transaction also included the City of Memphis acquiring [AutoZone Park](/wiki/AutoZone_Park "AutoZone Park") and then leasing it to the team.[[11]](#cite_note-2014sale2-11) Ron Warner led his club to a first-place finish (79–64), clinching the American Conference South.[[41]](#cite_note-BR2014-41) They were defeated in the conference series, three games to one, by Omaha, who later won the PCL title.[[41]](#cite_note-BR2014-41) The 2015 club, under manager [Mike Shildt](/wiki/Mike_Shildt "Mike Shildt"), finished in second place (73–71), two games behind the [Round Rock Express](/wiki/Round_Rock_Express "Round Rock Express").[[42]](#cite_note-BR2015-42)

The Cardinals sold their majority interest in the team to [Peter B. Freund](/wiki/Peter_B._Freund "Peter B. Freund") of Trinity Baseball Holdings in March 2016.[[3]](#cite_note-FrontOffice-3)[[43]](#cite_note-43) Memphis ended the 2016 season in fourth place with a 65–77 record.[[44]](#cite_note-BR2016-44) Prior to the 2017 season, the Redbirds unveiled new logos and uniforms. The primary logo is designed to look like a [neon sign](/wiki/Neon_sign "Neon sign"), such as those seen on nearby [Beale Street](/wiki/Beale_Street "Beale Street"), consisting of the team name and a redesigned image of team mascot, Rockey the Redbird. A secondary logo uses similar neon tubing to form an "M" in the shape of a [music note](/wiki/Music_note "Music note") to honor the city's [blues](/wiki/Blues "Blues") and [rock 'n' roll](/wiki/Rock_%27n%27_roll "Rock 'n' roll") heritage.[[45]](#cite_note-45) Led by [PCL Manager of the Year](/wiki/PCL_Manager_of_the_Year "PCL Manager of the Year") [Stubby Clapp](/wiki/Stubby_Clapp "Stubby Clapp"),[[46]](#cite_note-46) the 2017 Redbirds clinched the division title with a 91–50 record.[[47]](#cite_note-47) They went on to defeat the [Colorado Springs Sky Sox](/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Sky_Sox "Colorado Springs Sky Sox"), 3–2, to win the American Conference championship.[[48]]

[Christian Michelsen](/wiki/Christian_Michelsen "Christian Michelsen"), Prime Minister of Norway from 1905 to 1907, played a central role in the peaceful separation of Norway from Sweden on 7 June 1905. A national referendum confirmed the people's preference for a monarchy over a republic. However, no Norwegian could legitimately claim the throne, since none of Norway's noble families could claim [royal descent](/wiki/Royal_descent "Royal descent").

The government then offered the throne of Norway to Prince Carl of Denmark, a prince of the Dano-German royal [house of Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Glücksburg](/wiki/House_of_Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Gl%C3%BCcksburg "House of Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Glücksburg") and a distant relative of Norway's medieval kings. São Paulo's population has grown rapidly. By 1960 it had surpassed that of [Rio de Janeiro](/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), making it Brazil's most populous city. By this time, the urbanized area of São Paulo had extended beyond the boundaries of the municipality proper into neighboring municipalities, making it a metropolitan area with a population of 4.6 million. Population growth has continued since 1960, although the rate of growth has slowed.[[113]](#cite_note-113)

In 2013, São Paulo was the most populous city in Brazil and in South America.[[114]](#cite_note-114) According to the [2010 IBGE Census](/wiki/Brazilian_Institute_of_Geography_and_Statistics "Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics"), there were 11,244,369 people residing in the city of São Paulo.[[115]](#cite_note-115) Portuguese remains the most widely spoken language and São Paulo is the largest city in the [Portuguese speaking world](/wiki/Portuguese_speaking_world "Portuguese speaking world").[[116]](#cite_note-116)
